### What does this PR do?

Add a full-weight HCCL adapter for the public `HCCLTrainerWeightTransferEngine.trainer_init(..., client=..., source=...)` and `send_weights()` API. A replica leader sends to the next TP replica so the sender NPU does not also receive in the same HCCL group. This builds on the opt-in dispatch, IPC support and coordinated preflight from the preceding PR.

This is part 2 of a three-PR series. Depends on #8516. The branch targets upstream main and includes the preceding commits; review the incremental change [here](https://github.com/yeyunu/verl/compare/262e93a62860a0852ede39295e9e7b93448c0ecb...6168a527efae1f82ddb79478449ad76d93058bc2). Rebase after the prerequisite merges before merging this PR.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs: [Ascend weight](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+ascend+weight), [HCCL](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+HCCL), [IPC](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+IPC), [reload_weights](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+reload_weights). Checked on 2026-11-03 against main `2bcc98a9`.
- [x] Title follows `[rollout, vllm] feat: ...`.

This does not duplicate #8272 / RFC #7787: those implement **delta-sharded** HCCL; this integrates Ascend's official full-weight trainer/worker APIs. #7366 hardens the existing bucketed receiver protocol, #7920 handles oversized CPU tensors in the shared sender, and #5619 / #5378 add double buffering / slicing. This series leaves that shared sender unchanged and does not implement their features. #8507 updates the NPU patch layer, not these trainer-to-worker API adapters.

### Test

```bash
python -m pytest -q tests/workers/rollout/test_ascend_native_weight_transfer_on_cpu.py tests/workers/rollout/test_ascend_weight_update_preflight_on_cpu.py tests/workers/rollout/test_weight_update_dispatch_on_cpu.py
```

**85 passed on this branch** (Windows, Python 3.13, CPU torch 2.14.1). These tests execute the actual protocol/control-flow functions with device/Ray collaborators replaced; tensor operations and ZeroMQ are real. They do not establish real CUDA IPC or NPU collective correctness. The complete three-commit tree additionally passed the same 116 tests on Linux with CPU torch 2.10.

Ruff 0.12.2 check/format, license checks and `git diff --check` passed for each commit. On the complete series, full-tree Ruff and the available pre-commit sanity hooks passed; `mypy --platform linux` passed for all 709 tracked Python files. Linux runs of test-layout, documentation, license, device/DataProto usage, example naming, uv-policy, compileall and `bash scripts/generate_trainer_config.sh` passed.

`pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure` was also run on Windows: it is **not reported as fully passing**. The remaining failures are Linux-only `signal` attributes in unchanged reward code, Windows path separators in the existing test-layout allow-list, and shell Python resolution for the config generator. The corresponding checks were verified with Linux semantics as described above. A5 could not download the pre-commit hook repositories, so a complete default Linux pre-commit/CI run remains required.

Earlier downstream Ascend integration exercised one complete Step5 training step per interface and fixed-checkpoint parameter/output parity. This is supporting evidence from a model-enabled downstream checkout, **not** an NPU end-to-end pass on this rebased upstream branch.

### API and Usage Example

```bash
+actor_rollout_ref.rollout.engine_kwargs.vllm.weight_transfer_config.backend=hccl \
  +actor_rollout_ref.rollout.engine_kwargs.vllm.additional_config.weight_nz_mode=0
```

Use a compatible vLLM/vLLM-Ascend pair exposing the documented native APIs. This first version supports unquantized full weights; LoRA/QAT, a separately synchronized MTP drafter and delta payloads are rejected on the opt-in path. IPC/reload requires same-device colocation. HCCL additionally requires one node, replicated FSDP full-weight streams, at least two TP replicas, DP=PP=1 and no prefill/decode disaggregation. Native communication failures invalidate the adapter; restart workers before retrying. Default unconfigured paths retain their existing behavior.

### Design & Code Changes

- Extend the selector and worker preflight for `hccl`.
- Materialize bounded batches on the actor thread; keep FSDP iterator advancement there, and run the native engine on a dedicated thread with its NPU device selected.
- Adapt synchronous client RPCs to Ray. Start once, defer per-batch finish, and finish once after the full stream. Clone exporter-owned tensors before advancing the source.
- Reuse the trainer engine between rounds. Queue cleanup behind outstanding work on cancellation; do not claim that Python cancellation interrupts an HCCL collective.
- Add HCCL protocol/failure/cancellation tests and topology documentation.

No Step5 model implementation, private checkpoint/data paths, training diagnostics, SGLang changes or NPU worker patches are included.

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read the [Contribute Guide](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) and `AGENTS.md`.
- [ ] Complete the default Linux pre-commit / upstream CI run; local checks and platform limitations are recorded above.
- [x] Add documentation in `docs/ascend_tutorial/en/feature_support/native_weight_updates.md`.
- [x] Add CPU tests under the existing `tests/**/test_*_on_cpu.py` workflow discovery; no extra accelerator workflow was added.
- [ ] Human submitter reviews every changed line and runs the relevant paired-version NPU validation before marking ready for review.
- [ ] Request upstream CI approval through the repository process when ready. No Slack/Feishu message was sent.

@@ -0,0 +1,97 @@
+# Native vLLM-Ascend full-weight updates
+
+Last updated: 11/03/2026.
+
+These optional adapters delegate model loading to vLLM-Ascend. Leaving the
+options below unset preserves verl's existing weight path, including CUDA/ROCm
+IPC, shared-memory fallback and delta updates. The selector does not import
+`torch_npu` or `vllm_ascend`. Selecting an Ascend backend on another device is
+an error; it does not silently fall back to a different transport.
+
+## Requirements and scope
+
+Use a compatible pair of vLLM and vLLM-Ascend revisions. Verify Ascend's
+`.github/vllm-main-verified.commit` for the intended release rather than combining
+arbitrary main branches. This adapter requires the public native weight-transfer
+lifecycle and the packed consumer with a `device_index` argument; it is not a
+compatibility shim for older releases. Preflight checks callable signatures on
+the trainer and workers before starting the stream.
+
+The supported payload is a checkpoint-format, unquantized full-weight stream.
+LoRA, quantized/QAT models, a separately synchronized MTP drafter, shared-memory
+IPC fallback and `wire_format="delta_flush"` are rejected on this opt-in path.
+Set `additional_config.weight_nz_mode: 0` as required by Ascend's native update
+API. No model-specific adaptation or worker monkey patch is installed here.
+
+## NPU IPC
+
+```yaml
+actor_rollout_ref:
+  rollout:
+    engine_kwargs:
+      vllm:
+        weight_transfer_config:
+          backend: npu_ipc
+        additional_config:
+          weight_nz_mode: 0
+```
+
+The trainer packs a bounded byte buffer and exports a fresh IPC reference for
+each nonempty message. The worker calls `init_weight_transfer_engine`,
+`start_weight_update`, `update_weights` for each bucket, then
+`finish_weight_update` once. The official consumer owns independent copies;
+the trainer reuses storage only after acknowledgement and synchronization.
+An empty final message exports no unused IPC reference.
+
+IPC requires colocated trainer/rollout workers on the same physical NPU.
+`checkpoint_engine.update_weights_bucket_megabytes` controls buffer capacity.
+A single tensor larger than the bucket is sent directly, is not sliced, and
+must already reside on the sender buffer device. It stays alive until the ACK.
+Consequently memory use is bounded by the bucket plus the largest exported
+tensor and the official loader's own retained storage, not by the bucket alone.
+
+## Failure handling
+
+Preflight errors are collected across trainer ranks before receivers wait for
+data. A stream failure marks the adapter invalid; restart the rollout workers
+before retrying rather than generating with partially updated weights.
+IPC sends an explicit abort between requests and bounds socket operations at
+300 seconds. An outstanding native collective or crashed process still depends
+on runtime timeouts and the job supervisor; this is not in-place recovery.
+
+## Validation
+
+CPU tests use real PyTorch tensors and ZeroMQ, with substituted device/Ray
+collaborators. They cover stream ownership, mixed dtypes, empty/oversized tensors,
+failure/abort ordering, preflight and unchanged default dispatch. The existing
+CPU workflow discovers the `tests/workers/rollout/test_*_on_cpu.py` files.
+CPU dispatch tests do not establish real CUDA transfer correctness.
+
+The implementation was exercised in a downstream Step5 environment on Ascend:
+one complete training step per path and a fixed-checkpoint comparison against
+the previous loading path. Those results are prior integration evidence, not an
+end-to-end pass on this rebased upstream commit. Re-run with the intended model
+and paired dependencies before merging. Do not infer convergence from one step
+or compare independent training runs as though their final weights were equal.
+
+## HCCL
+
+Select `engine_kwargs.vllm.weight_transfer_config.backend: hccl` instead of
+`npu_ipc`. This adapter requires `HCCLTrainerWeightTransferEngine.trainer_init`,
+`HCCLTrainerInitInfo`, a client and a replayable source, plus `send_weights` and
+`shutdown`; it does not use the former static-send API.
+
+The initial supported topology is one node, replicated FSDP full-weight
+streams, at least two TP replicas, and inference DP=PP=1, with no prefill/decode
+disaggregation. A replica's trainer leader sends to the next replica so the
+source physical NPU is not also a receiver in its HCCL group. Other ranks still
+consume the exporter to participate in FSDP gathers. This does not implement
+the delta-sharded checkpoint engine or a general multi-node M-to-N transport.
+
+The trainer materializes one bounded batch on its actor thread and invokes the
+official engine on a device-bound transport thread. Start is forwarded once,
+per-batch finish calls are deferred, and finalization occurs only after the full
+stream succeeds. Producer tensors are copied before advancing a potentially
+reusing exporter. A single oversized tensor can exceed the batch limit.
+Cancellation queues cleanup after the outstanding transport call; it cannot
+interrupt a stuck HCCL collective. Persistent groups are reused between rounds.

+    """Provide import-only substitutes; tensor operations and ZeroMQ stay real.
+
+    Never import verl's rollout package initializer: it requires an installed

+    ]

+    for name, module in modules.items():
+        module.__path__ = []
+        parent, _, child = name.rpartition(".")
+        if parent in modules:
+            setattr(modules[parent], child, module)
+    device = modules["verl.utils.device"]
+    device.get_device_id = lambda: 0
+    device.get_device_name = lambda: "cpu"
+    device.get_torch_device = lambda: SimpleNamespace(synchronize=lambda: None)
+    device.is_support_ipc = False
+

+"""Select an opt-in weight update mode without importing accelerator packages."""
+
+from collections.abc import Mapping
+
+
+def _config_value(config, key):
+    if isinstance(config, Mapping):
+        return config.get(key)
+    return getattr(config, key, None)
+
+
+def resolve_weight_update_mode(config) -> str | None:
+    """Return the requested native mode, or None to preserve the legacy path.
+
+    Selecting a mode does not validate device availability. The native adapter
+    must check its platform, dependencies, and supported topology before starting
+    either side of a transfer. Other vLLM backends keep their existing behavior.
+    """
+    vllm_config = _config_value(_config_value(config, "engine_kwargs"), "vllm")
+    transfer_config = _config_value(vllm_config, "weight_transfer_config")
+    backend = _config_value(transfer_config, "backend")
+    return backend if backend in ("npu_ipc", "hccl") else None
